clarifications: Can node values be negative? Yes, they can be between -1000 and 1000.
Is the tree binary? Yes, it is a binary tree.
Can the tree be empty? Yes, it can be empty.
Are duplicate node values allowed? Yes, duplicate values are allowed.
What should the output format be? The output should be a string that can be deserialized back to the original tree structure.
Should the output be human-readable? No, readability is not required as long as deserialization works.
Should the tree structure be preserved exactly? Yes, structure must be identical after deserialization.
expectedApproaches: Preorder traversal with null markers, O(n) time and space.
Level-order traversal (BFS) with null markers, O(n) time and space.
solutions: Use a preorder traversal to serialize the tree, marking null children with a special character. Deserialize by reading the string and reconstructing the tree using the same traversal order.
Use a level-order traversal to serialize the tree, marking null children with a special character. Deserialize by reading the string and reconstructing the tree level by level.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to handle null children in serialization.
Not reconstructing the tree in the correct order during deserialization.
Using in-order traversal, which does not preserve structure uniquely.
edgeCases: All nodes have the same value

hintLadder.text: How would you traverse the tree to capture its structure?

Use a special marker to denote null children in your serialized string.
